title: The design argument
examples: Does evolution disprove the design argument?

explain.say: Imagine you are walking across a heath and find a watch on the ground. Its springs and gears fit together to tell the time, so you would conclude someone designed it. That is the picture William Paley painted in 1802.

Paley's argument goes like this. A watch has parts working together for a purpose, so it has a designer. Living things, like the eye, have parts working together even more wonderfully. So nature too has a designer, God.

items: A watch's parts work together for a purpose
So the watch has a designer
The eye is even more intricate
So nature has a designer: God

draw.text: It is also called the teleological argument, from the Greek telos, purpose.

explain.say: Even before Paley wrote, the philosopher David Hume had raised objections. The universe is not much like a machine. It might have had many designers, or a clumsy one. And a world with flaws and suffering does not point clearly to a perfect God.

items: The universe is not much like a watch
Why one designer, not a team?
We have seen watches made, never worlds

explain.say: In 1859 Charles Darwin offered a different explanation. Through natural selection, living things that happen to suit their surroundings survive and pass on their traits, so over millions of years they look designed without a designer planning each part.

items: More are born than can survive
The best suited survive and reproduce

explain.say: Many believers reply that evolution could be the way God designs, like a law God set in motion. A newer version, the fine-tuning argument, points out that the laws of physics seem set within narrow limits that allow life at all.

a: Tiny changes, no stars or life
b: We could only observe one that allows life

explain.say: So the design argument starts from a real sense of wonder at how well the world fits together. Whether that order points to a designer is still debated by believers and non-believers alike.

items: 1200s: Aquinas's fifth way, order points to an intelligence
1802: Paley's Natural Theology and the watch

faq.a: The design argument says that the order and purpose we see in nature, like the way the parts of an eye work together, are best explained by an intelligent designer, God. It is also called the teleological argument, from the Greek word telos, meaning purpose or goal.

In his book Natural Theology of 1802, William Paley said that if you found a watch on a heath, its working parts would show it had a maker. He argued that living things, such as the eye, are even more complex and fitted to a purpose, so they too must have a maker, God.

faq.q: Does evolution disprove the design argument?
faq.a: Darwin's theory of natural selection explains how living things can come to look designed without a designer planning each part, which removed Paley's main example for many people. But many believers say evolution could itself be God's way of creating, so they see no contradiction. The debate continues.

faq.q: What were Hume's objections to the design argument?
faq.a: In his Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion, published in 1779, David Hume argued that the universe is not very like a machine, so the comparison is weak. He added that design might suggest many gods or an imperfect god, and that we have never watched a universe being made, so we cannot judge.

The fine-tuning argument says that physical constants, such as the strength of gravity, fall within narrow ranges that allow stars, planets and life to exist. Supporters say this is best explained by a designer. Critics suggest there could be many universes, or that we could only ever find ourselves in one that allows life.

Natural selection is the process Darwin described: living things vary, more are born than can survive, and those best suited to their surroundings survive and have offspring, passing on their traits. Over very long times this can produce eyes, wings and other complex features.

Intelligent design is a modern movement claiming that some features of living things are too complex to have evolved step by step, so they point to a designer. Most biologists reject it as science, and a United States court ruled in 2005 that it could not be taught as science in public school science classes.
asks: what do scientists think of intelligent design

faq.q: Who first made the design argument?
faq.a: The idea is ancient. Thinkers in ancient Greece and Rome, such as Cicero, argued from the order of the heavens to a divine mind, and Thomas Aquinas's fifth way in the 1200s argued that things without intelligence act toward goals, as an arrow is aimed by an archer. Paley made the most famous version.

faq.q: Do other religions use the design argument?
faq.a: Yes. The Qur'an often invites people to reflect on the signs of God in the heavens, the earth and living things, and many Jewish, Christian and Hindu thinkers have seen order in nature as pointing to God. Buddhism generally does not focus on a creator.

faq.q: If the world was designed, why does it have flaws?
faq.a: This is a major objection: disease, wasteful parts of bodies and natural disasters seem odd for a perfect designer. Believers reply that a world of stable natural laws allows both good and harm, or that flaws come from a fallen world. This links to the problem of evil.
asks: why is nature cruel if designed

faq.q: What did Richard Dawkins say about design?
faq.a: In his 1986 book The Blind Watchmaker, the biologist Richard Dawkins argued that natural selection is like a watchmaker with no foresight, building complex life by tiny steps with no plan. He saw this as answering Paley without a designer.

faq.q: Does the design argument prove God exists?
faq.a: Philosophers disagree. Supporters find the order and beauty of the universe a strong pointer to a designer; critics think natural selection, chance or many universes might explain it. People weigh the evidence differently, which is why the argument is still discussed.
asks: strengths and weaknesses of the design argument

facts: William Paley published Natural Theology, with the watchmaker analogy, in 1802.
David Hume's Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion, criticising design arguments, was published in 1779.
Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species, describing natural selection, in 1859.
The design argument is also called the teleological argument, from the Greek telos, meaning purpose.
Thomas Aquinas's fifth way argues from order in nature to an intelligent director.

quiz.say: Recall. In Paley's famous comparison, what object is found lying on a heath?
quiz.show: What did Paley imagine finding on a heath?
quiz.why: Paley imagined finding a watch, whose working parts show it had a maker, and compared it with living things.

wrong.0: Paley said a stone might have lain there forever; it is the watch that shows design.
wrong.2: A book is not Paley's example.
wrong.3: The eye is what Paley compared the watch to, not what was found on the heath.

quiz.say: Apply. A biologist explains how the eye could develop step by step over millions of years, each step helping survival. Which thinker's idea is this?
quiz.show: The eye developing step by step through survival: whose idea?
quiz.why: This is natural selection, Darwin's explanation for how complex features can appear without a designer planning each step.

wrong.1: Paley argued that the eye shows a designer, not that it evolved.
wrong.2: Aquinas lived centuries before evolution was proposed.

quiz.say: Think. A believer says, I accept evolution, and I think God designed the laws that make it possible. What does this reply do?
quiz.show: Evolution as God's method: what does this reply do?

options.show: It moves design from each creature to the laws of nature
options.say: It moves design from each creature to the laws of nature

quiz.why: Instead of saying God designed each creature directly, this reply says God designed the laws and processes, such as evolution, through which life develops.

wrong.0: The believer accepts evolution, so does not reject it.
wrong.2: It is a way of fitting belief with science, but it is not a proof.
